title: Use coverage as a clue
summary: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well.
introduction: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain use coverage as a clue
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("both signs", () => { const positive = n => n > 0; expect(positive(2)).toBe(true); expect(positive(-1)).toBe(false); });
blocks.title: Use coverage as a clue

blocks.text: Both checks state a result. A coverage report is useful alongside these expectations.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: High coverage is not a guarantee of correct behaviour.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
